differential.name: Acute Pyelonephritis
differential.icd10: N12.6 (Pyelonephritis, acute, with other specified complications)

supporting_evidence.finding: Elevated WBCs in urine (>100/μL), positive leukocyte esterase, and nitrite test.
Patient reports severe flank pain, fever >38.5°C, nausea, and vomiting.
CT scan shows right renal enlargement with perinephric stranding indicative of inflammation.

differential.reasoning: Combination of clinical symptoms (flank pain, fever), urinalysis findings (WBCs, leukocyte esterase, nitrite), and imaging results (CT showing renal inflammation) strongly support acute pyelonephritis.

differential.name: Nephrolithiasis with Infection
differential.icd10: N13.6 (Hydronephrosis due to calculus, complicated by infection)

supporting_evidence.finding: Urine culture pending, but urinalysis consistent with infection.
CT scan shows right renal calculus and hydronephrosis.

differential.reasoning: Presence of a renal stone (nephrolithiasis) with associated hydronephrosis, combined with urinalysis suggesting infection, makes this diagnosis plausible but less likely than acute pyelonephritis given the severity of symptoms and imaging findings.

differential.name: Other Differential: Renal Infarction

supporting_evidence.finding: No clear evidence of renal infarction on CT, but cannot be completely ruled out.

differential.reasoning: Though imaging does not clearly show renal infarction, it remains a low-probability differential due to the severity and acute nature of symptoms.

clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with severe flank pain, fever, nausea, vomiting, and urinalysis indicative of infection. Imaging shows renal enlargement and perinephric stranding consistent with acute pyelonephritis. Differential diagnosis includes nephrolithiasis complicated by infection but is less likely given imaging and symptom severity.
